class_guess: Bell eats counter: BECv5 TM1/TM2's counter with F1 = 1LF; the counter alternates std / packed encodings, with dirty transients
summary: BECv5 TM1/TM2 counter; F1=1LF packs the top pair. Halting only at rare dirty overflows, avoided by >= 0.29 m.
mechanism: K(w,n,m) = w <A 1(10)^(1+n)0(10)^m. Each bounce applies phi to w (last 00 -> 1, zeros to its right; F1 = 1LF lets a carry pass 11) and moves one 10 from n to m. At n = 0 the right side eats the counter's low end (template ROv).
The counter comes back shifted one cell and recounts, so it alternates encodings: std(N) -> pk(2k+b) -> std(2r+b) ... In 2.8% of cycles the overflow sees a dirty word, still shifted.

Halting needs an odd landing at a dirty overflow ending 01/11 (or 10, nested). None in 17M cycles (~5e22 steps), gap >= 0.29 m. No 740 holdout shares the table; 349 is equivalent (TM518) to it started in F.

history.skeleton: 0^inf w <A 1100 (10)^m 0^inf, w = std(N) | pk(N) | dirty word

rules.name: init
rules.cases: via K('',0,0) at step 5 and K('',1,0) at step 14; = std(1), m = 1

rules.name: R1 bounce
rules.cases: n >= 1; phi(w): last cell 0 -> 1, else the last 00 pair (0^inf counts) -> left cell 1, all cells right of it 0 (random w up to 14 cells)

rules.name: R2 overflow, q even
rules.cases: phi(w) = x 1 0^q with q even (the template's ROv when w = std((2k+1)2^i-1): q = 2i, x = std(k)0)

rules.name: R3 overflow reset, q odd
rules.cases: phi(w) = x 1 0^q, q odd, x = x' 00 or x empty

rules.name: R4 overflow halt
rules.cases: phi(w) = x 1 0^q, q odd, x ends in 01 or 11; never reached from blank (17M cycles)

rules.name: B std -> pk
rules.cases: N = (2k+1)2^i - 1, b = 1+i+m, L = bitlen(k); clean iff k a power of 2 or 2k+b >= 2^(L+1); k = 0: std(b); else dirty phi^b(std(k)0)

rules.name: B pk -> std
rules.cases: k = 2^(L-1)+r, r > 0, clean iff 2r+b >= 2^L; k a power of 2: std(k+b); k = 0 (all ones): reset, then std(b+1), m = b+1; else dirty phi^b(pk(k)0)

rules.name: phi^j acceleration
rules.cases: cells below the lowest 1 at an odd offset count in binary on their even offsets; when full, the next step lands above

template.note: Kept: LC0, R n m, LInc0, LIncs, RIncs, ROv for std counters. New: a packed counter pk with its own ROv/increments, the shifted-counter orbit (replaces LIncs': H0 -> pk(2k+j) / std), dirty transients, reset R3, and the invariant.

strategy: Find an invariant on (type, N, m) at overflow, plus the dirty state, that keeps b' off the odd landings ending 01/11/10 (measured gap >= 0.29 m). Then copy BECv5 TM1's LC0/R/RIncs/ROv, add pk lemmas and the dirty-orbit lemma, and close with progress_nonhalt_cond.
risks: No invariant yet: the halting branch is real in the abstract system, so a proof must pin down N vs m tightly enough.
Dirty orbits need a recursive word description (binary sub-counters on even offsets) that is heavier to formalize than BinInc.
R3 resets (hit once, near misses at distance 2) put non-standard words into the next overflow; the invariant must cover them.
